tasks.task: Find a news article on BBC News about the impact of the recent tech industry layoffs on the global economy. Summarize the key points and the name of the author, and provide the date of publication.
tasks.answer: Article: 'Are tech job cuts a warning for the wider economy?' by Natalie Sherman, published 6 January 2023. Key points: A wave of job cuts hit major US tech firms in late 2022/early 2023: Amazon axed 18,000 workers (6% of office staff), Salesforce cut ~8,000 (10%), with similar announcements from Meta, Cisco, and Stripe. Tech executives blamed over-hiring during the pandemic boom; higher interest rates, dried-up start-up funding, and the crypto sector meltdown also contributed. Economists (Julia Pollak of ZipRecruiter, Joe Brusuelas of RSM) viewed the cuts as a correction after an era of excess, not the start of a systematic recession. The broader US labour market remained strong: employers added 223,000 jobs in December 2022 and unemployment fell to a historic low of 3.5%. The tech layoffs were seen as more of a warning sign (a 'canary in the coal mine') for the global economy than for the US economy; the IMF warned a third of the world economy would contract in 2023.

tasks.task: Identify the latest health-related news on BBC News and summarize the main findings or recommendations.
tasks.answer: The latest health-related news on BBC News is 'I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work', published 2026-10-30 (BBC Health section, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm78pxxe55v0o). Main findings: 23-year-old special educational needs teacher Saskia Reeves-Priestley collapsed at work with dizziness, nausea, heart palpitations and feeling hot; blood tests showed her vitamin D level was 'next to nothing'. Vitamin D deficiency is increasingly widespread in the UK, especially among young people - nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient last year according to the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, with girls and young women particularly affected. Most vitamin D is made by the body when UV sunlight hits the skin (diet sources like oily fish, meat and supplements contribute less); reduced sunlight, covering skin, sunscreen and darker skin tones all lower production. Deficiency is linked to rickets in babies and osteomalacia (bone weakening) in adults. Recommendations: get safe sunlight exposure, consider dietary sources/supplements of vitamin D (doctors will offer supplements to high-risk patients who are concerned), and be aware symptoms can be difficult to spot and easily missed.
